description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—on the Llama2 model across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^4 (10,000), with major tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, 10^3, and 10^4. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is on a linear scale from 60% to 80%, with tick marks at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) shows a gradual upward trend, starting near 61% at 10^0 and reaching approximately 67% at 10^4. “FT” (blue line with downward triangle markers) begins at about 63% and rises steadily to around 69% at 10^4, exhibiting moderate growth. “IKE” (red line with upward triangle markers) starts at roughly 65% and increases to about 70% by 10^4, plateauing after 10^2. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers) begins near 66%, climbs to ~72% at 10^2, and stabilizes near 74% at 10^4. “MEMIT” (purple line with pentagon markers) starts at ~66%, rises to ~71% at 10^2, and reaches ~73% at 10^4, showing slightly lower performance than MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers. “ROME” (green line with square markers) begins at ~72%, increases to ~76% at 10^2, and plateaus near 78% from 10^3 to 10^4, consistently outperforming all other methods across the entire range.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) on Llama2 across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, with MEMIT slightly surpassing MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falling behind at higher values. FT demonstrates the steepest growth rate, increasing by nearly 10% across the range, while Base remains relatively stable, showing minimal improvement. IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
